item.content:encoded:
I typed out a whole bunch more stuff and then cut like a fiend so bear with me here.

There are no victories, no end game, no better world to be created by such analysis. Only a circular firing squad where power is purchased by complaint.

That's not true. Out there in the wide world, such analysis can and has done good. It's silly to claim otherwise just because it's also been used to enable control freaks and assholes.

That's missing the point though!

I gave the critique to try and help Aelanna make a better joke SCP article, and that's it.

If, for me, the joke fell a bit flat because of the associations with a cliche, shitty joke (women suck at tech lololol), then I should say so.

I'm not using it to make myself look morally superior or to purchase any kind of power (and I couldn't; the author is an IRL woman in tech which means she trumps me in these games, and no one in this community gives a shit about earning self-righteousness points… at least not that kind).

Imagine if I'd flipped out on you when you critiqued my clumsy use of a rape trope way back when. CALL THE INTERNET POLICE, WE HAVE A JAILBREAK

but to imply one is more amusing than the other because its too gauche to make a joke around a female character… tsk. Jokes are for everyone and on everyone.

Nope, I didn't even imply that you can't make jokes about girls, and I strongly oppose such an idea. As do the vast majority of people who care about those topics, although we get accused of supporting such outlandish crap all the time and it's just. so. tiresome.

Anyway people use non-gender/race-based critique to beat people with like cudgels all the time. But you haven't gone down the road of "Stop The Goodreads Bullies" quite yet.

So why should we make special effort to never analyze or point out gender/race-based cliches? Setting up artificially taboo topics because some people somewhere else on the internet are shits about those topics makes no sense. This is just as bad as censoring willy-nilly just in case imaginary people are offended.

item.content:encoded:
Torn on this one. It's a witty execution of a really boring joke… which would be enough for me usually, but too much of the content is still cliched.

Not sure how to fix, though. Making her a him? (Typically this joke is about a woman, and by extension all women, being terrible at tech.) Making her something besides an anthropology researcher? (The role fits the cliche joke perfectly — adds a mockery of the so-called 'soft sciences' — but in real life would be a sign of an extremely bad anthropologist… or maybe that's meant to be part of the joke, IE it's why she can't resist clicking on everything to 'study' it? But that seems off point.)

(at this point I feel like I'm analyzing an urban myth Snopes-style)

Maybe it would just be fix if it was slightly funnier overall — unfortunately, TL333s's quote reminds me that this joke was funnier when Homestar Runner did it. Although TL333's other quotes are pretty funny (as well as Addendum 1938-3, although what Mary actually wrote was a leetle too similar to the fat man joke SCP)… but taking all bits of the article together, it doesn't quite make the grade for me.

No vote for now.
